notes.title: Controller Support Is Here!
notes.content:
Ahoy me lovelies! 🦜

Controller support for Anchored Hearts has arrived!!! ☀️🏝️

Give the game a spin on a controller. I have been enjoying the ship battles on a controller! 🎮⛵💥

If you love the game, please leave a review or encourage a friend to do so. If we get 7 more reviews, we will be able to receive a Positive (or Mixed) label, which can make a big difference. As a small indie, it would mean a lot to us to get to 10.

This is the last major update we have planned. Anchored Hearts was a labour of love for our team, and we hope you have enjoyed going on this journey with us. Our focus is now fully on the next game, and we hope to see you on the next adventure!

Fair winds and good controllerin'! ☠️

notes.title: Controller Support incoming for Anchored Hearts
notes.content:
Ahoy me lovelies! 🦜

While we have been busy working on our next game, we have not forgotten about you! Alex, who is both the designer and programmer on Anchored Hearts, has been hard at work on controller support for this game that we poured our hearts into.

Turns out adding controller support was a lot trickier than we first thought, due to various boring technical reasons. So I can only say that Alex has been an absolute hero braving the storm on a single float in the middle of the ocean to get it in!

And now it's land ahoy! ☀️🏝️

We are just running our last few tests and you'll be able to play with a controller in the next few days!

Enjoy the Spring Sale, and we hope you'll enjoy controller support when it's ready!

Arrrr! Fair winds and good sailin'! ☠️

notes.title: Our first itty bitty update
notes.content:
Ahoy me lovelies! 🦜

This is our very first update to Anchored Hearts, and we're patching a bunch of little bugs! Arrr!

- Fixed a bug where the player could LMB mash the battle fire button very fast and cause it to not fire again until un- and re-hovered
- Tweaked up cannonball speeds to avoid them being too fast or too slow at either end
- Fixed a (harmless) crew rehire bug where finishing with less crew than you started with could cause negative numbers on the rehire UI
- Bird tweak to flapping pattern
- Tweaked nav recenter speed to make it less vertigo-inducing, it's snappy now, also increased manual scroll speed, and fixed a tiny bug where recentering to the start would not disable the back scroll button
- Fixed character fade animation playing when it ought not to at the end of story scenes which finish with a narrator line
- Fixed a Battle tutorial typo
- Nav tutorial updated slightly because the Shipyard exists and Boons can be bought at sea (how did we ever live without these features 😭)
- Romance music wasn't set to return to town music on a specific romance choice with Xander, now it does
- Desktop icon has finally been fixed (you won't believe how long it took to figure out the problem and it was so easy in the end!)
- Little Dialogue fixes such as making a different background appear and a typo

Fair winds and good sailin'! Arrrr! ☠️

notes.title: Anchored Hearts Released!
notes.content:
Ahoy me lovelies! 🦜

At long last, [i]Anchored Hearts: A Tale of Destiny[/i] is now ready to play! ✨

Our little team has poured a lot of love into this game over the past year, with many trials and tribulations along the way... but finally here it is.

When we first started on [i]Anchored Hearts[/i], we knew what we wanted to make an adventure about a "pirate queen", with heart-throbbing romance, written by Anna and Catherine. But it didn't stop there for us, because any game published by Lovewish has to have more than story alone. Alex and Lorna worked hard to develop an early prototype for what now have become our ship battles... and so the foundation of [i]Anchored Hearts[/i] bloomed into existence.

Over the year that followed, we worked hard to bring the narrative together with the gameplay, while at the same time allowing each to stand on its own merit.

With passion come fiery discussions, as the team drank [strike]rum[/strike] beverages, threw dice at each other, and covered an eye with an eyepatch. There were even [strike]unrelated[/strike] injuries that knocked out our UI artist! High drama! (OK only about half of that is true.)

Many times over the past year, we were not sure if the combination of narrative + ship battles would make people happy, or put them off. Would the battles be too much for people who prefer visual novels? Would the narrative be too much for people who prefer roguelites?

But we took the game to events and saw people play it, and wow we were blown away by the response. At one event, someone played the demo from start to finish, and told everyone on the bus home how much they loved it - so the next day all their friends turned up to play it too! 💖 It was so touching and really meant the world to us that something we made was loved so much.

We set sail into the unknown, and it has been a long voyage for us. There have been calm seas, and stormy seas, but we hauled our treasure all the way here, and now we dock at the port to share our treasure with [i]you[/i].

Hope you have a great time playing [i]Anchored Hearts: A Tale of Destiny[/i] and please leave a review to let us know what you think!

Arrrr! Fair winds to ye! 🦜

notes.title: Devs Chat and Play Anchored Hearts!
notes.content:
Join us during the June Steam Next Fest for our second live stream, as we play through the Anchored Hearts demo, including some chats with our dev team! Watch us navigate wild waters, fight enemy ships, and meet our potential love interests.

Chat with us and get a taster for what the game has to offer!

Features:
A gripping narrative mystery
Romance multiple characters
Navigate a roguelite map
Engage in epic real-time ship battles
Buy or earn ship upgrades as you build notoriety
